picks.style: archaic greek hymn, phorminx lyre and low drone, rhapsode tenor, stately, incantatory, processional
picks.why: The Muses washing in the spring and dancing on soft feet before they go abroad by night, veiled in mist.

picks.style: cold underworld chant, bowed drone and distant bell, low male voice, very slow, vast, echoing
picks.why: The great gulf where a falling man needs a whole year to reach the floor, and Night and Day greet each other on the bronze threshold.

picks.style: thunderous epic chant, deep drums and low brass drone, massed male voices, fast, cataclysmic, roaring
picks.why: Zeus opening on the Titans — the sea seething, heat seizing Chaos, earth and heaven sounding as if hurled together.

picks.style: georgian nocturne, harp and low strings, soft female voice, hushed, moonlit, slow
picks.why: 'At this lone hour, when Nature silent lies' — and Hydra-headed Care drops his galling chain for one moment.

picks.style: melancholy english art song, viola and piano, low female voice, brooding, spare, unresolved
picks.why: 'I sicken at the Sun, and fly his beams, / Like some sad ghost which loves the moonless night.'

picks.style: gothic ballad, harpsichord and tremolo strings, urgent female voice, eerie, quick, shivering
picks.why: A reader frightened by her own book — the fleshless form rising as the taper sinks, in tight singable quatrains.

picks.style: english work song, bare frame drum and fiddle, plain strong female voice, steady, driving, unadorned
picks.why: 'No Learning ever was bestow'd on me; / My Life was always spent in Drudgery' — the whole address lands in ten lines.

picks.style: winter labour ballad, low fiddle and hand drum, weathered female voice, slow, cold, insistent
picks.why: Rising under Orion in the snow while 'you on easy Beds may lie and sleep' — the contrast is the song.

picks.style: kitchen work chant, clattering percussion and drone fiddle, rough female chorus, brisk, relentless, wry
picks.why: Pots, kettles, saucepans, skillets, skimmers and ladles — a catalogue that beats like a work rhythm, ending on lost perfections.

picks.style: english pastoral air, recorder and harpsichord, light soprano, gentle, springlike, lilting
picks.why: An invitation sung to birds — hop from spray to spray, weave the mossy nest, sing the live-long day.

picks.style: reflective baroque air, solo lute, quiet tenor, slow, still, meditative
picks.why: The stream and the hour-glass in eight lines: 'each falling sand his folly chides, / Who lets one precious moment run to waste.'

picks.style: georgian song of absence, guitar and viola, warm male voice, plaintive, unhurried, evening-toned
picks.why: Larks and flowery fields turned unbearable by one absence — 'Sick of the world I muse alone.'

picks.style: latin drinking incantation, hand drums and low pipes, chanting male voices, insistent, hypnotic, accelerating
picks.why: The only candidate, and it is already a chant: 'Drink thrice' opening and closing a hammering litany of threes.

picks.style: french baroque funeral air, viol consort and chamber organ, grave baritone, slow, dignified, austere
picks.why: The epitaph at its centre stands alone — wandering, poor, banished, and even his ashes hidden from the wolves.

picks.style: early latin saturnian chant, plucked lyre and hand drum, rough low voice, archaic, measured, sparse
picks.why: The old Ennian praise of Cethegus — 'the chosen flower of the people, and the marrow of Persuasion.'

picks.style: latin epigram song, single lute and light hand percussion, wry tenor, light, quick, brief
picks.why: One barbed image, whole in itself: phrases laid like the little cubes of a mosaic pavement.
